notes: οὐκ … εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα → *never*: the single English word goes to the negator and the three duration tokens are unrepresented, on rule 48's reasoning applied by analogy to οὐκ rather than οὐ μή. Stretching *never* over the phrase is the rejected reading. A reference comparison will report those three tokens as disagreements.
αἰωνίου ἁμαρτήματος → *an eternal sin*: both words anarthrous, so the determiner and the case preposition belong to the noun (rules 21, 58).
